labels.notes: No mark. The tools/ledger.py regex \*\*`(prefix:...)`\*\* finds nothing in the first 4000 characters. The only bold-backtick run in the whole file is a prose heading. The docstring says '**Not marked**' and the REPORT row is partial, which is correct: the file builds the model X_0 = E0 and not the paper's E^{1,2}_A-spacetimes (T-ett-singular-sfa, OQ-34, OQ-35 disclosed). On the structure. E0GX.singularGX is the maximal a.e. (Flat.isom 2, Minkowski 2)-atlas of the sector atlas, with IsMaximalAEAtlas proved. That is exactly DEC-25's 'maximal a.e. (G,X)-atlas, a (G,X)-atlas on a portly subset' (strict SingularAtlas.lean l.1539; IsGXAtlas means one g per connected component of an overlap). It is not vacuous: Sing = axis is nonempty, and every sector chart is in the atlas. On Reg = axis^c. reg_eq is right, and so is source_inter_axis_eq_empty. A chart of the maximal atlas at an axis point p would, on a slit box around p, be g1·(sector chart at +1) and g2·(sector chart at −1). Those two sector charts agree on the upper half-box and differ by hol(2π) on the lower one. Rigidity then gives g2 = g1 and g2 = hol(2π)·g1, so hol(2π) = 1, which is impossible because hol(2π) moves nullToMink(0,1,0). I re-derived it by hand: the angles are arg z and π + arg(−z), equal for Im z > 0 and 2π apart for Im z < 0. On the holonomy. In null coordinates (a,b,c) = (t+x, t−x, y), the form is −ab + c². angleShift s preserves it: (a − 2sc + s²b)b vs (c − sb)². (A−1)³ = 0, and A ≠ 1 for s = 2π. So isParabolic_holLin_two_pi is true, with a pure nontrivial unipotent, which is stronger than the library's IsParabolic needs. The fixed set {b = c = 0} is the developed axis, as in gx's btzHol. sectorChart_eq_zpow_smul_on_component gives one k for the whole connected component: the local k, then rigidity against the component's single g. On hreg. E0GX.chartIso_of_mem_aeAtlas has exactly the form of hreg in existsUnique_causality_singularGX_dec25 (GXSingularDEC25.lean l.551) at the model E0, with DY = E0.causality and DX = minkowski 2. On the model-free lemma. chartIso_of_mem_maximalAEAtlas_of_agreeOn is true (kernel) and strong enough for hreg at κ = 0, through forall_chartIso_aeAtlas_of_reg_subset with reg_eq and support_sectorAtlas. Its added hypothesis (DX absolutely minimal on its open sets) is disclosed and follows from DEC-25's (a). On Finding 1 (roadmap). The counterexample refutes exactly the roadmap wording. A = {id on C∖{0}} is an a.e. atlas for the translations (ℂ∖{0} is portly). Its chart is a ChartIso segCausality{0} → segCausality∅, since a segment inside U ⊆ ℂ∖{0} avoids 0. Translations are strong morphisms of segCausality∅. Both causalities are AbsolutelyMinimal and AbsolutelyMinimalOn every open set, by a Lebesgue subdivision against the library's AbsolutelyMinimalOn (Generated.lean l.239); the lt half is vacuous because lt = False. segCausality satisfies every field of Causality. refl ℂ is in the maximal atlas and is not a ChartIso, since [−1,1] passes through 0. The local IsRigidAction (Multiplicative ℂ) ℂ is true (translations are affine, via the strict isRigidAction_of_affine) and hides nothing: the statement of counterexample does not even depend on it. On the Isom reading, see the findings: l.1401 forces time-orientation preservation only.

findings.what: The paper finding misdescribes the paper. It says the paper 'states this fact nowhere and cites no source for it' (that E0's (Isom(E),E)-structure does not extend across the line). But ETT.tex:1331, inside the very lines cited, says 'its singular locus {r=0} is a lightlike line'. Under DEC-25 that is the statement that the structure does not extend. The subsection opener (l.1322–1324) also gives blanket sources [thesis, hal-01317447, brunswic2021cauchy]. What is true, and Lean-proved (source_inter_axis_eq_empty, reg_eq, hol(2π) ≠ 1), is narrower: the paper asserts this without an argument, and without the precise reference that l.1324 promises for each fact. Sent as worded, the finding would tell the author something false about the text.
findings.fix: At graduation, reword to: 'ETT.tex:1331 asserts that {r=0} is E0's singular locus. Under DEC-25 this means the (Isom(E),E)-structure of reg(E0) does not extend across the line. That holds because the holonomy about the line is the parabolic hol(2π) ≠ 1 (Causal.E0GX.source_inter_axis_eq_empty, reg_eq). The paper gives no argument and no precise reference for it (l.1324 promises one per fact); one sentence would do.'

findings.what: The Isom question overstates what the paper forces. Its argument is right for time orientation. With the full O(1,2)⋉R³, T∘sectorChart (T a time reversal) is in the maximal a.e. atlas and is not a ChartIso to minkowski 2, so hreg fails, and the group does not act by morphisms (l.1401). But l.1401 forces only the orthochronous group Isom^↑ = O^↑(1,2)⋉R³, not 'Isom_0'. Spatial reflections preserve Minkowski's causal and chronological relations. With Isom^↑, the maximal atlas gains mirrored sector charts, which are ChartIsos; hreg still holds, and so do Reg = axis^c and the action by morphisms. So Isom_0 (Flat.isom 2 = SO0(1,2)⋉R³, the library's existing reading in Remarks/MassiveManifold) against Isom^↑ is a genuine reading for the author: it decides whether non-orientable singular flat spacetimes are admitted. The paper's own hypothesis does not settle it.
findings.fix: Reword the question: l.1401 forces time-orientation preservation (Isom^↑); restricting further to the identity component Flat.isom 2 is a reading; ask the author which of the two is meant.

findings.what: E0GX.isRigidAction_isom and its `attribute [local instance]` are redundant. The strict library already has the global instance Causal.Flat.isAnalyticAction_isom (Causal/Flat/Developing.lean:140), which is in this file's import closure. `#synth IsRigidAction (Flat.isom 2) (Minkowski 2)` after the file returns `Flat.isAnalyticAction_isom.toIsRigidAction`. The SCOPE bullet (l.79–80) and kb_proposals[0] ('IsRigidAction (Flat.isom 2) (Minkowski 2) is the theorem E0GX.isRigidAction_isom, to make local') suggest the instance is missing. It is not. The REPORT notes also expect a possible sibling rigidity theorem; none exists.
findings.fix: At graduation, delete isRigidAction_isom and l.322; it is harmless, since it is a Prop. Drop that clause from the SCOPE bullet and from kb_proposals[0].

findings.what: Placement and restatements, for graduation. The model-free section (MaximalAEAtlasIso) and AESupportCounterexample sit in a module that imports the E0 model. Roadmap item (3) asked for an ETT-layer or Port module so that T-ett-ealpha-gx-structure can reuse them, and kb 0047 says a layer-1 module may not import a model. The dispatch allowed this single file, so the closer is not at fault. Two gx lemmas are restated under the model namespace E0GX, both disclosed and both verified against lean-gx/GX/Singular/Quotient.lean: E0GX.isPreconnected_ball_diff_zero (l.2260, verbatim) and E0GX.isPortly_ne_zero (l.2284, at Z = ℝ, with mem_setOf_eq dropped from one simp only). They are generic topology, and the counterexample already uses the first outside E0GX. Separately, the sibling EAlphaSectors.lean's EAlphaSector.chartIso_of_compatible uses the same agree-locally argument at chart level (groupoid hypothesis, source in regPart). That is a merge candidate, not a duplicate: different name, different type. MassADEC25.lean duplicates nothing here. Its SCOPE remark that the library has 'no singular structure on' the E_κ becomes stale once this file graduates.
findings.fix: At graduation, hoist MaximalAEAtlasIso, AESupportCounterexample, isPreconnected_ball_diff_zero and isPortly_ne_zero (renamed out of E0GX) into a model-free module beside Causal.GXSingularDEC25 or Causal.Port.Portly. Consider deriving EAlphaSector.chartIso_of_compatible from the model-free lemma.
